# zeta-lab

> A computational laboratory for the Riemann zeta function: verified numerics,
> runnable demonstrations, and a written course covering the Riemann Hypothesis
> from the harmonic series to the research frontier. It is an instrument for
> building intuition, **not** a proof attempt — nothing computed here is
> evidence for RH, and `docs/08` explains why no computation could be.

Everything is Python + mpmath/Arb, tested against independent oracles. The
organising idea: theta is the heat kernel, Poisson summation gives its modular
identity, the Mellin transform turns that into the functional equation whose
mirror axis is Re(s) = 1/2, the explicit formula rebuilds the primes from the
zeros, and running the same heat flow on Ξ produces the de Bruijn–Newman
constant, where RH ⟺ Λ = 0 and Λ ≥ 0 is a theorem.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): front door — quickstart, what to run first, repo map.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): operating context for coding agents — setup, house
  rules, naming traps, honest-scope policy. Read before changing anything.
- [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md): the decisions — strategic bet, deliberate
  non-goals, known gaps, next build. Read before planning work.
- [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md): generated index of the full API, docs, scripts and
  test counts. Regenerate with `python scripts/make_context.py`.

## The written course (docs/, in reading order)

- [docs/00-orientation.md](docs/00-orientation.md): what RH says, what is known, honest scope.
- [docs/01-sums-integrals-and-continuation.md](docs/01-sums-integrals-and-continuation.md): the harmonic series, Euler–Maclaurin, ζ(−1) = −1/12.
- [docs/02-theta-heat-and-modularity.md](docs/02-theta-heat-and-modularity.md): theta as the heat kernel; Poisson summation.
- [docs/03-functional-equation.md](docs/03-functional-equation.md): modularity in, ξ(s) = ξ(1−s) out.
- [docs/04-explicit-formula.md](docs/04-explicit-formula.md): zeros ↔ primes as an identity.
- [docs/05-de-bruijn-newman.md](docs/05-de-bruijn-newman.md): heat flow on Ξ; RH ⟺ Λ = 0.
- [docs/06-hilbert-polya-and-gue.md](docs/06-hilbert-polya-and-gue.md): the spectral dream and random-matrix statistics.
- [docs/07-equivalences-and-criteria.md](docs/07-equivalences-and-criteria.md): statements equivalent to RH.
- [docs/08-why-it-is-hard.md](docs/08-why-it-is-hard.md): what each known technique provably cannot do.
- [docs/09-new-ontologies.md](docs/09-new-ontologies.md): what "RH needs new mathematics" means.
- [docs/10-trace-formulas-and-connes.md](docs/10-trace-formulas-and-connes.md): explicit formula as a trace formula.
- [docs/11-f1-and-the-missing-geometry.md](docs/11-f1-and-the-missing-geometry.md): the field with one element; Deninger.
- [docs/12-how-hard-problems-die.md](docs/12-how-hard-problems-die.md): how famous problems actually get solved.
- [docs/13-moments.md](docs/13-moments.md): external zero windows, finite moments, leading constants, and gated scorecards.

## The conjecture factory (`discovery/`)

- [discovery/README.md](discovery/README.md): design document for the discovery
  funnel — five candidate kinds, six verdict states, the deduplication contract,
  what the schema cannot express, and the historical validation. A pipeline that
  logs itself so the conversion rate per generator can be measured: on a fresh
  ledger, 26 candidates → 20 already known, 1 trivial, 5 inconclusive, 0
  survivors. Run it with `scripts/13_discovery_run.py`.
- The seam: `schema/registry/ledger/funnel/metrics/historical_cases` are
  domain-agnostic and import nothing from `zeta`; `discovery/domains/` is the
  only place the subject is named. Enforced by tests.
- Honest scope: a survivor is a **lead**, never a result and never evidence for
  RH; "not recognised offline" is the absence of a lookup, never novelty; the
  ledger in `conjectures/` is gitignored and must never be published.

## Optional

- [references/papers.md](references/papers.md): annotated reading list.
- `scripts/`: numbered runnable demonstrations; `06_tour.py` runs the whole
  story in about ninety seconds.
- `figures/`: generated plots; rebuild with `scripts/make_figures.py --quick`.
